title: Prove quasipolynomial bound for chronological batch widths (no new κ)
body:
PR #4507 constructs smaller chronological batch widths but leaves their all-rank growth bounded only by the inherited `exp(O(N log N))` estimate. This package proves, for every **fixed** rule in #4436's default-height flow,
`log B_N = O((1+log N)^(d+2))`,
where d counts distinct primes dividing target or paid ranks. For raw p7, d=7, giving `B_N = exp(O((1+log N)^9))`. This answers the upper-bound part of [the #4503 handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4503#discussioncomment-19117802). No new κ.

The proof combines strict fractional rank descent, the exact prime-valuation recurrence for `B_e/gcd(B_e,q)`, and a source-state lemma: the default-height flow changes only at products of primes from the fixed rank alphabet. In particular, `B_n | L_N^D(n)`, where `L_N` is the LCM of source totals through rank N. This is a new bound on #4507's existing width sequence, not a new batching policy or a finite-rank improvement. The bound is loose: at p7 rank 1,000 its binary exponent is 303,840, while the existing actual width has 2,524 bits.

Only `research/chronological-width-growth/` is added. Start with its [proof and scope](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/aadb7bc59390683450b1969e4632f546929dc569/research/chronological-width-growth/README.md) and [exact receipt](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/aadb7bc59390683450b1969e4632f546929dc569/research/chronological-width-growth/RESULT.json). The new valuation/breakpoint checker uses an authenticated copy of #4507's flow/width generator as the object being studied; it does **not** claim a second independent implementation of that generator.

Validation on CPython 3.12.0 / Windows, standard library only:

- 1,074 compiled ranks and 49,474 actual batch constraints: exact valuation equality, fractional rank descent, source-LCM envelope, and all pinned final width hashes.
- 832 cutoff cases, including 642 nontrivial comparisons with a smaller smooth representative; full flow equality also checked across each floor-cutoff interval.
- Ten rejection controls, including a paid-prime omission counterexample, new width primes outside the rank alphabet, and failure when the depth factor is dropped.
- Registered ordinary and optimized replays pass. Four external source/receipt/code corruption controls reject.
- Final-commit byte preflight and 14-file export integrity pass. The exported verifier passes with `-I -O -B`, Git unavailable, socket creation disabled, and unchanged payloads.

```sh
python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/chronological-width-growth
```

Limitations: the universal conclusion comes from the written proof, not extrapolation of the finite checks. Constants depend on the fixed rule. No matching lower bound, polynomial width, changed-height #4483 application, generation-time bound, physical/native admission, or new normalized leaf cost is proved. The optional source-history preflight requires full history and was unavailable in the shallow checkout; all pins are at the canonical-main base. The orientation-only baseline stopped on a sparse-omitted selected claim file. No selected cold replay, formal proof kernel, independent human review, or hosted-CI pass is claimed.

Started from canonical main `f626db5c3a3d781d8f7695038776c621651f75e1`, priority revision 7, unchanged on the final fetch. Refreshed overlap covered all 5,860 tracked local note paths, 357 open PRs and 3,489 Discussion records with reported complete pagination at 08:07–08:08 UTC on October 22. #4519 already recounts finite widths; #4476/#4521 cover different old-width/expanded-count obligations. This explicitly changes the independent-moment card to the live compiler-width handoff.

Credit Jacob Alan Sussman, zxv, Cinna Davis, Ryanson Jonathan, Mihir Srivastava's #4507 and the retained native/outer lineage. Prepared for **Mihir Srivastava / mihir-s-05 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, without subagents or independently launched reviewers. Apache-2.0. Selected frontier unchanged.


Hosted CI update: the planning job failed on four unchanged current-status/navigation tests before package selection; the package replay was skipped. The same four failures reproduce locally. See the [exact-head CI evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4586#issuecomment-6336170463). Local scientific passes are separate.
